# Using Leak Guard in Kiro

<!-- Generated by `node packages/cli build` from the harness registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

The skill is the same in every agent. This guide covers only what is specific to Kiro.

## Install

Project scope (one repository): copy this skill folder to `.kiro/skills/leak-guard/`.

User scope (every project): copy it to `~/.kiro/skills/leak-guard/`.

From the gti-skills repository, the CLI does the copy for you:

```bash
node packages/cli install --harness kiro --skill leak-guard
node packages/cli install --harness kiro --skill leak-guard --scope user
```

Restart the agent session after installing so it rescans its skills.

## Use

Describe the task in plain language. Kiro loads the skill when the request matches its `description`. You can also run it explicitly by typing `/leak-guard`.

## Where the skill finds its files

`<skill-dir>` in `SKILL.md` is the folder that contains `SKILL.md`: `.kiro/skills/leak-guard` for a project install, or `~/.kiro/skills/leak-guard` for a user install. Scripts and references are always addressed relative to it.

## Verify

Ask the agent which skills it has loaded and check that `leak-guard` is listed.

## Notes

- Workspace skills take priority over user skills with the same name.
- This skill drives packages/leakguard. Read scripts/leakguard.root for the absolute package path; if you copied the skill folder by hand without the install command, locate packages/leakguard in the gti-skills repository and use its bin/leakguard.mjs and bin/leakguard-hook.mjs paths.
- The guard installs as a command hook (preToolUse) in .kiro/hooks/leakguard.json or ~/.kiro/hooks/leakguard.json.
- Documentation: [Kiro](https://kiro.dev/docs/skills/) (path source: official).
